transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to review the exhibition protocol today. As you know, six student portfolios have been selected for the district's annual public art exhibition at the central library, and I need to approve the final protocol before it goes out to the library and participating families. Let's start by going through the draft plan together. I understand it proposes displaying the work in the central library foyer, publishing an online gallery, labeling pieces with students' full names, and returning or discarding the original portfolios after the exhibition. I'd like to hear your thoughts and any concerns you have with each element before we finalize anything.

transcript.text: I need to raise a serious concern. When I was reviewing the consent forms for all six selected portfolios during this week's portfolio selection, I found that they permit public display only in a staffed indoor gallery, require student initials rather than full names on labels, and prohibit online publication. I verified all of this but I have not yet transferred those restrictions into the draft plan. This means the current draft conflicts with the consent forms on three points: the foyer display may not qualify as a staffed indoor gallery, the online gallery is not permitted, and labels must use initials instead of full names.

I have not yet updated the exhibition paperwork to reflect this, so we need to revise the draft to ensure the originals are transferred to the archive instead of being returned or discarded.
